title: Internal: Suggestions beta readiness review (flags, runbooks, support) — go/no-go
summary: Internal go/no-go review for the Console Suggestions view beta (read-only). Team reviewed feature-flag/allowlist readiness, tenant isolation/RBAC and audit logging, telemetry freshness and stale-estimate behavior, runbooks + alert thresholds, Support enablement/FAQ, and the proposed staged rollout to a small cohort. Main open risks: (1) savings estimate volatility when baselines age or traffic is spiky, (2) guardrails for showing/withholding suggestions under insufficient telemetry, and (3) ensuring the tenant scoping fix is fully verified in prod-like conditions. Outcome: conditional go pending final checks (staging verification, SRE dashboards wired, Support FAQ published, and security sign-off on audit log fields).
topics: Rollout scope: read-only beta + allowlisted cohort
RBAC permissions and audit logging for Suggestions read access
Telemetry freshness SLO and stale estimate detection
Runbooks, dashboards, and incident criteria during beta
Support readiness: FAQ, escalation path, weekly feedback loop
Known limitations and customer messaging (risk vs confidence)
action_items: Chloe Martin — verify tenant scoping regression test passes in staging and run a prod dry-run with two workspaces (due 2026-02-19)
Logan Wright — confirm baseline freshness job and stale-estimate metric are emitting in prod; share dashboard link in #announcements (due 2026-02-19)
Rafael Mendes — finalize alert thresholds for stale estimates + 5xx rate and add incident pause criteria to the runbook (due 2026-02-20)
Dev Patel — publish Support FAQ + canned responses for savings variability and 'insufficient telemetry' state; align with Marissa/Aditya copy (due 2026-02-20)
Naomi Feldman — confirm security review items: audit log fields, retention, and RBAC scope; send final 'OK to enable cohort' note (due 2026-02-20)
Leila Farouk — run E2E gating test suite in CI against release candidate and report any remaining flakes (due 2026-02-19)
Connor O'Brien — coordinate enablement window on release train; draft rollback comms template for #eng-releases and #support (due 2026-02-20)
Rachel Kim — finalize first cohort list + owner mapping (CSM/SE) and book 30-min onboarding slots (due 2026-02-21)
next_steps: Complete final staging/prod-like verification of allowlist gating + tenant scoping + RBAC
Lock dashboards/alerts and confirm on-call rotation knows pause/rollback steps
Publish Support FAQ and internal enablement guide link for CSM/SE
Enable beta for 2–3 pilot tenants first, then expand to remaining cohort over 48–72 hours if stable
Hold first weekly beta check-in and review: adoption, estimate stability, and top support tickets
transcript:
Meeting title: Internal: Suggestions beta readiness review (flags, runbooks, support) — go/no-go
Recorded: 2026-02-18 10:02 AM PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Talia Benson, Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin, Logan Wright, Rafael Mendes, Dev Patel, Rachel Kim, Naomi Feldman, Leila Farouk, Connor O'Brien

---

[00:00] Talia Benson: Alright, folks, thanks for hopping on. Goal today is basically go/no-go for enabling the Suggestions beta cohort. We’re still read-only. We’re checking flags, runbooks, support plan, and any “please don’t ship this” risks. If we’re green we’ll schedule the enablement window with releases.

[00:24] Dylan Brooks: Sounds good.

[00:25] Chloe Martin: Yup.

[00:27] Talia Benson: I’m going to drive off the checklist. First: feature flag and allowlist. Dylan or Chloe, can you confirm what’s in prod?

[00:36] Chloe Martin: So the BFF has gating on suggestions_beta. And then per-tenant allowlist check. The admin tool writes the allowlist entry to the config service, and the BFF reads it. In staging it’s wired; in prod the flag plumbing is deployed, but we’ve not turned on the flag globally, obviously.

[01:01] Dylan Brooks: And client side has the same flag so nav item doesn’t show. If you manually hit the route without being allowlisted, you get the “not enabled” empty state, not a 404.

[01:13] Talia Benson: Okay. Any gotchas there? Like caching of the allowlist value.

[01:19] Chloe Martin: There is caching. It’s like 60 seconds. We can lower it for the first day if we want, but then we’ll add load to the config API. I think 60 is fine.

[01:30] Connor O'Brien: Just to be clear, changing that TTL would be a code change, not a config change, right?

[01:35] Chloe Martin: Correct. Not doing that unless needed.

[01:39] Talia Benson: Good. Second: tenant isolation and the scoping bug we saw in staging. Chloe, where are we on that?

[01:49] Chloe Martin: We found it. It was a missing workspace_id filter in one join path for “detail” reads, not list reads. Fixed and added a test. But I want to re-run it with two workspaces that share a parent org because that’s what triggered it.

[02:09] Naomi Feldman: Just to note, that’s the one I care about most from security. If there is cross-workspace visibility even read-only, that’s unacceptable.

[02:18] Dylan Brooks: Totally.

[02:19] Talia Benson: Let’s treat that as a hard gate. Chloe, you’ll do the staging verification and a prod dry-run? Like with two internal workspaces.

[02:28] Chloe Martin: Yes. I can do that tomorrow morning.

[02:31] Talia Benson: Great. Next: RBAC and audit logs. Naomi, can you summarize where we landed?

[02:39] Naomi Feldman: Sure. RBAC: we’re scoping view access to a permission that maps to “Optimize: view suggestions.” For beta we’re allowing Org Admin and Billing Admin by default, but not plain “Developer.” That’s consistent with showing cost/usage-derived insights.

[03:00] Naomi Feldman: Audit logging: we log suggestion_read events with tenant/workspace identifier, actor, and suggestion_id. We are not logging the full savings payload, because that includes derived metrics that could be sensitive and it bloats logs. We do log a hash of the schema version and recommendation type.

[03:21] Dev Patel: Wait, support asked if they can see why someone saw “insufficient telemetry.” Will they need the full payload?

[03:29] Naomi Feldman: That should be in application logs, not audit logs. Audit logs are for “who accessed what,” not for debugging.

[03:38] Logan Wright: Plus the telemetry basis is already in the UI drawer—like “data window last 7 days, N requests, baseline updated X hours ago.” Support can ask the customer to screenshot that.

[03:52] Dev Patel: Right, okay.

[03:54] Talia Benson: Connor, do we have the audit log deployment confirmed in prod?

[03:59] Connor O'Brien: Yes, it’s on the release train already. I’ll double check the migration or whatever… but I think it’s just writing to the existing pipeline.

[04:08] Dylan Brooks: No migration. It’s a new event type.

[04:11] Connor O'Brien: Great.

[04:12] Talia Benson: Next: telemetry freshness and stale estimates. Logan, can you give us the current behavior?

[04:20] Logan Wright: The savings estimates use baselines derived from token metering, per route/model. We compute and cache daily-ish, but for beta we’re trying to keep it within 6 hours for high-traffic tenants. There’s a freshness timestamp included. If the baseline is older than 24 hours, the UI will show a banner: “Savings estimate may be stale.”

[04:43] Talia Benson: And do we hide suggestions if it’s stale?

[04:47] Logan Wright: No. We debated that. Right now we show them with the banner and drop confidence in the estimate. The “risk” level is separate, but the detail drawer has a section that basically says “basis of estimate.”

[05:02] Dylan Brooks: We also added the “insufficient data” empty state when we literally don’t have enough requests in the window. That’s separate from stale.

[05:11] Rafael Mendes: From SRE standpoint, I like not hiding stuff silently. But we need a clear incident threshold if the whole thing goes stale because some pipeline job broke.

[05:22] Logan Wright: We have a stale_estimate_ratio metric. It’s “percent of suggestions served with baseline_age > 24h.” Right now it’s only in staging dashboards.

[05:34] Talia Benson: So gating item: confirm that metric is in prod and on dashboards. Rafael, you’re going to set thresholds.

[05:42] Rafael Mendes: Yep.

[05:43] Rachel Kim: Can I ask a question? Some customers are going to see week-over-week changes even if nothing changes, right? Like traffic mix changes.

[05:52] Logan Wright: Yes. The baseline is a moving window. We can message that.

[05:56] Dev Patel: That’s one of the top support concerns. People will be like “you said $900, now it says $300.”

[06:03] Dylan Brooks: The drawer shows confidence interval, not just one number.

[06:08] Dev Patel: But do they notice it…

[06:10] Talia Benson: Let’s talk about messaging under Support plan.

[06:13] Talia Benson: Before that—runbooks. Rafael, can you walk through what’s ready and what’s missing?

[06:20] Rafael Mendes: Sure. We have dashboards: suggestions-service p95, error rate, and a panel for stale estimate ratio. We added links to runbooks: “Suggestions beta” runbook includes steps to disable the feature flag globally, and steps to remove a tenant from the allowlist.

[06:41] Rafael Mendes: Missing piece is we haven’t aligned on incident criteria. Like what counts as “pause beta.” My proposed: if 5xx > 2% for 10 minutes, pause. If stale ratio > 30% for 1 hour, pause. If we get any confirmed cross-tenant data leak, immediate pause and incident.

[07:04] Naomi Feldman: Yes. That last one is non-negotiable.

[07:08] Dylan Brooks: Agreed.

[07:10] Talia Benson: Okay. Rafael, can you add those criteria to the runbook. Also, who’s on point for the first 72 hours?

[07:18] Rafael Mendes: Standard SRE on-call will get alerts, but I’d like Logan or someone from telemetry to be tagged for stale estimate alerts.

[07:26] Logan Wright: That’s fine. Put me as secondary.

[07:29] Talia Benson: Connor, any release risks? We had some CI flakes from E2E tests.

[07:36] Connor O'Brien: Yeah, E2E selectors were flaking. Leila has been stabilizing. From release standpoint, enabling the flag is low risk, but we don’t want to do it on the same day as like a major console deploy.

[07:51] Leila Farouk: The flakes are down but not zero. The “empty state” test fails maybe 1 in 20. I changed to data-testid, but there’s still a timing issue.

[08:04] Dylan Brooks: That might be the skeleton loader delay.

[08:06] Leila Farouk: Exactly.

[08:07] Talia Benson: Leila, can you run the suite against the RC and report by tomorrow? If we still have 5% flake rate, we can’t use it as a gate.

[08:17] Leila Farouk: Yep.

[08:19] Talia Benson: Support plan. Dev, where are we?

[08:24] Dev Patel: We drafted the FAQ. We’ve got canned responses for: “why risk is high,” “why no suggestions appear,” “why savings changed,” and “what telemetry do you need.” We also have escalation path: first to TAM/CSM, then to #optimize-suggestions-beta channel, then on-call if it looks like a platform incident.

[08:47] Dev Patel: The thing we’re missing is final copy alignment. Some text says “estimated savings,” some says “projected.” We need one phrase. Also, we need to make sure support isn’t promising “you will save X.”

[09:01] Dylan Brooks: The UI itself says “Estimated savings.”

[09:04] Dev Patel: Great, we’ll match.

[09:06] Rachel Kim: For enterprise customers, they also ask “can you prove it for audit.” We need to say “these are projections based on your recent traffic.”

[09:15] Naomi Feldman: And “audit logs track access” but we don’t provide a full export of their usage in this UI. I’d like that in the FAQ.

[09:24] Dev Patel: Okay.

[09:25] Talia Benson: Rachel, beta cohort. Are we aligned on who gets it first?

[09:31] Rachel Kim: I have a list of eight accounts, mixed: two Dedicated, three Hosted, three Private-ish. But I propose we do a smaller initial set—two or three—so we can monitor. We’ll do onboarding sessions where we explain risk taxonomy and the “basis of estimate” section.

[09:49] Talia Benson: Perfect. Who are the first three?

[09:52] Rachel Kim: One dedicated enterprise with stable traffic, one mid-market with a lot of batching opportunity, and one internal dogfood workspace.

[10:04] Dylan Brooks: Internal dogfood is key. We should be able to see weird edge cases.

[10:08] Talia Benson: Any objections to staged rollout? First 2–3 tenants, then expand after 48 hours if stable.

[10:14] (all): No.

[10:16] Talia Benson: Cool. Now, outstanding risks. Let’s list them explicitly. I have: tenant scoping, stale/freshness, support messaging, and risk/confidence confusion. Anything else?

[10:31] Chloe Martin: One more: pagination and performance for large tenants. We added cursor pagination, but we haven’t tested with like 10k suggestions. Not in beta though.

[10:40] Dylan Brooks: Our current list view is paginated. For beta, suggestion volume shouldn’t be that high because we’re only generating for top routes.

[10:49] Logan Wright: Another risk: double counting when both caching and batching apply. That was fixed, but it’s worth validating with a sanity query.

[10:58] Talia Benson: Good call.

[11:00] Naomi Feldman: Also, privacy: the detail drawer includes “top route” and “region.” That’s okay for authorized roles, but if RBAC is too broad, it’s an issue. So RBAC needs to be correct.

[11:12] Dylan Brooks: RBAC check is at the BFF layer. If the UI somehow caches a response, it’s still gated.

[11:18] Naomi Feldman: Great.

[11:19] Talia Benson: Let’s drill into risk taxonomy vs confidence because that came up in feedback. Dylan, what’s in UI right now?

[11:27] Dylan Brooks: In the list, we show a “Risk” chip: Low, Medium, High. In the drawer, we show a few bullet rationales like “Latency headroom < 10% at p95” or “Cache hit-rate prediction uncertain.” There is also a “Confidence” field in the savings object but we’re not surfacing it as a separate chip; it’s included in the estimate range.

[11:49] Dev Patel: Support question: people interpret “High risk” as “unsafe” and then they don’t look. But sometimes it’s high risk because long context workload variance, not because it will break anything.

[12:02] Logan Wright: Yeah. We should emphasize reversibility: read-only now; later apply will have rollback.

[12:08] Rafael Mendes: The pause criteria should include if we see latency regressions correlated with adoption, but we’re not applying anything yet. So it’s mostly about data correctness, outages, and privacy.

[12:20] Talia Benson: Right, since read-only, the main risk is “we’re misleading” or “we leak.” Not “we broke their prod.”

[12:27] Chloe Martin: Unless the Suggestions endpoints create load. But they’re cached and not called super frequently.

[12:32] Rafael Mendes: We should still watch p95.

[12:35] Talia Benson: We will.

[12:37] Talia Benson: Okay, quick round: are we comfortable enabling for internal dogfood today if tenant scoping test passes? Or do we wait for all gating items.

[12:47] Dylan Brooks: I’d wait until we have dashboards in prod. If we enable and we can’t see metrics, that’s annoying.

[12:54] Logan Wright: Agree.

[12:55] Connor O'Brien: Also prefer doing it during a normal release window.

[12:59] Talia Benson: Okay. Target enabling window: Friday morning? That’s 48 hours from now.

[13:05] Connor O'Brien: Friday 10 AM PT is fine.

[13:08] Dev Patel: Works for Support.

[13:10] Rachel Kim: Works for CS. I can schedule the first onboarding early next week.

[13:15] Talia Benson: Great.

[13:16] Talia Benson: Let’s capture gating checklist for Friday enablement:
- Tenant scoping verification
- Prod dashboards for p95/5xx/stale estimate ratio
- Support FAQ published
- Security sign-off on RBAC + audit log fields
- E2E tests stable enough (or removed as hard gate)

[13:38] Leila Farouk: I’ll say we can keep E2E as informational if flakey. But we at least need the gating tests for allowlist / not-enabled state.

[13:48] Dylan Brooks: That’s reasonable.

[13:50] Talia Benson: Okay. Naomi, for security sign-off, what do you need?

[13:55] Naomi Feldman: I need confirmation that audit logs are emitted for both list and detail reads, and that RBAC denies are tested. Also, I want to confirm we’re not exposing raw token counts in the UI; it should be aggregated.

[14:10] Logan Wright: We show “requests in window,” not tokens. We do show $/1M tokens estimate and monthly impact, but not their exact usage.

[14:19] Naomi Feldman: Good.

[14:21] Talia Benson: Chloe, do we have audit logging on both endpoints?

[14:25] Chloe Martin: Yes, list and detail. It logs suggestion IDs returned. Though—small note—the list endpoint can return up to 50 IDs, so that’s a bigger audit record.

[14:37] Naomi Feldman: That’s fine.

[14:38] Dylan Brooks: Wait, does it log all IDs? That could be a lot.

[14:41] Chloe Martin: It logs a count and the first 10 IDs. Sorry, I said that wrong.

[14:46] Dylan Brooks: Okay, cool.

[14:49] Talia Benson: Perfect.

[14:51] Talia Benson: Anything else we should call out for known limitations in beta?

[14:57] Logan Wright: Suggestion generation is only for top routes and only for batching/caching classes. No quantization suggestions yet.

[15:06] Dylan Brooks: And there’s no apply button. We should make sure we’re not teasing “apply” too heavily.

[15:11] Dev Patel: The FAQ says “Phase 2 will include apply with guardrails,” but we shouldn’t commit to a date.

[15:18] Talia Benson: Right, no dates.

[15:20] Rachel Kim: Also, dedicated/private customers will ask “does this map to my deployment?” We should say “Suggestions are per route/model/region; for Private the UI still shows but data windows depend on telemetry integration.”

[15:33] Logan Wright: Yeah, Private telemetry can be delayed. That may trigger “stale.”

[15:38] Rafael Mendes: That’s an adoption risk. But we can keep Private out of first wave.

[15:43] Rachel Kim: Agreed.

[15:45] Talia Benson: Okay, let’s do a quick recap of decisions and assign owners.

[15:50] Talia Benson: Decisions:
1) Staged rollout: 2–3 tenants first, then expand after 48–72 hours.
2) Friday 10 AM PT enablement target, pending gates.
3) E2E tests are not a hard release gate if flaky, but gating scenarios must be validated.

[16:12] Talia Benson: Owners/actions (I’ll send this after, but let’s read out):
- Chloe: tenant scoping verification + prod dry run.
- Logan: prod metric emission and dashboard link.
- Rafael: thresholds + pause criteria in runbook.
- Dev: publish FAQ and canned responses.
- Naomi: final security sign-off after verifying audit + RBAC.
- Leila: RC test run and report flakes.
- Connor: coordinate release window and rollback comms.
- Rachel: finalize initial cohort and schedule onboarding.

[16:45] Dylan Brooks: One more thing: do we want a “kill switch” per tenant besides removing allowlist? Like a second flag.

[16:52] Chloe Martin: It’s basically allowlist removal. That’s our per-tenant kill.

[16:56] Rafael Mendes: That’s fine for beta.

[16:58] Dylan Brooks: Okay.

[17:00] Talia Benson: Any last concerns? Speak now.

[17:04] Dev Patel: Just… we should be prepared for “insufficient telemetry” tickets. If the customer has traffic but we’re not ingesting due to some lag, they’ll be confused.

[17:15] Logan Wright: We can add in the drawer the “last telemetry ingest time.” Not sure it’s in this build.

[17:22] Dylan Brooks: It’s not in the UI. But we have baseline updated time.

[17:26] Logan Wright: We can answer that in support escalation. For beta, that’s okay.

[17:31] Talia Benson: Okay. We’ll track first week tickets and see if we need UI change.

[17:37] Naomi Feldman: Also make sure support doesn’t ask customers to send logs with usage data. Just a reminder.

[17:43] Dev Patel: Yep, we’ll request screenshots of the basis panel, not raw logs.

[17:47] Talia Benson: Great.

[17:49] Connor O'Brien: For Friday, I need the go/no-go by Thursday EOD.

[17:55] Talia Benson: Understood. I’ll run an async check in Slack Thursday at 3 PM PT and we’ll decide.

[18:03] Dylan Brooks: Works.

[18:04] Talia Benson: Alright, thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.

---

Auto-generated notes (Fireflies):
- Key risks mentioned: tenant scoping regression, stale estimates and metric visibility, E2E test flakiness, support messaging on estimate variability.
- Next meeting: weekly beta check-in to review adoption + support issues (to be scheduled after enablement).
